themes_detail.label: Street Lighting Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Street light outages spiked to 28 complaints THIS WEEK—a 377% jump from the 5.9-per-week baseline—suggesting a widespread infrastructure failure in Morningside Heights/Hamilton Heights that could affect evening safety and pedestrian navigation.
evidence: 28 street light complaints THIS WEEK vs. 5.9-per-week 8-week average (377% spike, z-score: 6.23)
Statistically significant anomaly meeting high-severity threshold
Aligns with long-standing community board priority: 'Other capital request (DOT)' — repeated funding asks suggest chronic infrastructure underinvestment
reporting_angles: Contact DOT to identify which streets/intersections are dark and whether this reflects equipment failure, maintenance backlog, or a single incident
Interview residents about safety concerns from darkened streets; check whether crime reports or pedestrian incidents correlate with outage zones

themes_detail.label: Vendor Enforcement Surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor enforcement complaints jumped 800% THIS WEEK to 9 complaints versus a 1.0-per-week baseline, suggesting either a sudden enforcement push, street vendor density spike, or new quality-of-life complaints in commercial zones that warrant investigation.
evidence: 9 vendor enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0-per-week 8-week average (800% spike, z-score: 6.53)
Coincides with 237% spike in commercial noise complaints 3 weeks ago (93 vs. 27.6 avg), suggesting vendor-related disruption pattern
No recent news coverage or community board alerts found — story appears under-reported
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH and NYC Department of Consumer Affairs to determine if there is an active vendor enforcement operation or licensing sweep underway
Map vendor complaint clusters by street/intersection; interview local businesses and vendors about enforcement intensity and citation reasons

themes_detail.label: Street Noise Spike (Sidewalk)
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 144 THIS WEEK—a 327% increase from the 33.8-per-week baseline—indicating a potential new source of public disturbance (construction, street events, or commercial activity) warranting immediate identification.
evidence: 144 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 33.8-per-week 8-week average (327% spike, z-score: 4.96)
Accompanied by 237% commercial noise spike 3 weeks ago (93 vs. 27.6 avg), suggesting sustained commercial/street activity disturbance
368 DOB permit filings in last 90 days (mostly alterations) may indicate active construction projects generating noise
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 noise complaints with DOB permit filings to identify which construction or renovation projects are triggering complaints
Canvass affected blocks (likely near commercial corridors on Amsterdam Ave, Broadway, or 125th St) to identify specific noise sources and resident impact

themes_detail.label: Police Non-Emergency Complaints Spike
themes_detail.summary: Non-emergency police matter complaints jumped 324% THIS WEEK to 9 complaints from a 2.1-per-week baseline, potentially signaling a localized safety concern, disorder, or quality-of-life incident cluster requiring clarification.
evidence: 9 non-emergency police complaints THIS WEEK vs. 2.1-per-week 8-week average (324% spike, z-score: 6.53)
Occurred same week as street light outages and vendor enforcement surge, suggesting possible multi-factor neighborhood disruption
No constituent services data or recent news coverage available — signal underdeveloped
reporting_angles: Request NYPD incident logs and 311 complaint detail to identify the specific nature of non-emergency calls (loitering, dispute, trespassing, etc.) and geographic cluster
Interview precinct commander and local residents about whether this reflects a discrete incident or sustained pattern

themes_detail.label: Special Projects Inspection Spike
themes_detail.summary: Special Projects Inspection Team (SPIT) complaints spiked 1100% three weeks ago (6 vs. 0.5 baseline average), the highest z-score anomaly in the dataset, though recent-week data is unavailable—warrants confirmation of whether this spike has sustained or resolved.
evidence: 6 SPIT complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.5-per-week 8-week average (1100% spike, z-score: 11.0 — highest severity in dataset)
SPIT handles enforcement of illicit activities (unlicensed operations, illegal conversions); spike suggests targeted enforcement push or emerging violation cluster
Timing (3 weeks ago) predates this week's vendor enforcement and noise spikes — may represent early phase of broader enforcement cycle
reporting_angles: Contact DOHMH and Department of Buildings to determine what triggered SPIT deployment 3 weeks ago and whether it remains active
Identify specific addresses or blocks targeted for inspection; cross-reference with community board priorities around land use and illegal housing
